quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When leaving an alley or driveway to enter traffic, you should:

options.text: Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.
Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
Expect pedestrians to get out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
questions.explanation: You must stop before driving onto a sidewalk when leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot. Pedestrians and other traffic have the right-of-way.

questions.question: Alcohol is:

options.text: A stimulant.
An antihistamine.
A depressant.

questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your thinking and makes your reflexes slower.

questions.question: For drivers 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.05 percent.
0.08 percent.
0.02 percent.

questions.explanation: For drivers 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: The best way to avoid a dangerous driving situation is to:

options.text: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
Turn off the radio.
Always look straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always watch what is happening around you. Look ahead, to the sides, and behind your vehicle. This helps you spot problems early and make safe decisions about speed and position.

questions.question: If a child is about to run into the street, you should:

options.text: Start to slow down.
Flash your headlights.
Blow your horn sharply.

questions.explanation: Blow your horn sharply when a child or pedestrian is about to step into the street in front of you. This warns them of danger.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dark street, you should:

options.text: Drive slow enough to stop within your headlight beam.
Use high beam headlights to see vehicles ahead.
Keep your dashboard lights bright so others see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slow enough to stop within your headlight beam.
questions.explanation: Drive slower at night than during the day. You cannot see as far ahead. Make sure you can stop your vehicle within the area lit by your headlights.

questions.question: If you are about to be hit from behind, you should NOT:

options.text: Apply your brakes.
Let go of the steering wheel.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let go of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If hit from behind, press yourself against your seat and push your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and be ready to brake. Do not let go of the wheel.

questions.question: This yellow sign means:

options.text: One lane ahead.
Merging traffic ahead.
Lane ends ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic may merge into your lane ahead.

questions.question: You must give the right-of-way to pedestrians who are:

options.text: In a marked crosswalk.
In any crosswalk or intersection.
Crossing any street.

questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians crossing in any marked or unmarked crosswalk. For safety, yield to any person crossing the street.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Steep hill ahead.
Road construction area.
Road narrows ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns of a steep or long hill ahead. The hill may have sharp curves.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an upcoming corner. Who should you yield to?

options.text: Oncoming vehicles that are also turning left.
All vehicles coming toward you.
Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a "Walk" signal.

questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other vehicles that have a green light.

questions.question: You are driving in the left lane of a two-lane road. Many vehicles are passing you on the right. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in your lane so traffic flows smoothly.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let other vehicles pass.
Move to the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane for passing or turning left. Use the right lane when driving slower than other traffic, entering the road, or turning right.

questions.question: Which statement about work zones is true?

options.text: Fines for violations in work zones are the same as regular traffic violations.
You must slow down for the cone zone.
Slow down only if you see workers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down for the cone zone.
questions.explanation: Always reduce your speed in work zones and be ready to stop. Driving carefully through work zones protects drivers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and road workers.

questions.question: When is a rear-facing child restraint required?

options.text: For any child weighing 25 pounds or less.
For children one year old weighing 30 pounds or less.
For children under one year old weighing 20 pounds or less.

questions.correctAnswerText: For children under one year old weighing 20 pounds or less.
questions.explanation: State law requires children under age 16 to use proper child restraint systems. A rear-facing child restraint is required for children under one year old who weigh 20 pounds or less.

questions.question: When entering the interstate, you find a gap in traffic, match the speed, and signal. What is your next step?

options.text: Expect traffic to let you in because you have the right-of-way.
Merge carefully into the gap.
Wait for the lane to completely clear before merging.

questions.explanation: Find a gap, speed up to match traffic, signal, and then merge when safe. Do not expect other drivers to make room for you.

questions.question: The road ahead is covered with heavy smoke. What should you do?

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers and keep driving.
Slow down, move to the right, and stop off the roadway.
Turn on your high beam headlights and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to the right, and stop off the roadway.
questions.explanation: If heavy smoke covers the road, slow down immediately, drive as far right as possible, and stop off the roadway. Then check if it is safe to continue. Heavy smoke can hurt your eyes and lungs.

questions.question: A traffic signal shows a steady yellow light and you have not yet entered the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Slow down and proceed carefully through the intersection.
Come to a safe stop.

questions.explanation: When you see a steady yellow light before entering an intersection, stop safely. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through at a safe speed.

questions.question: How do you make room for cars entering the freeway?

options.text: Slow down.
Merge into a different lane.
Keep your speed and position the same.

questions.explanation: Make room for entering vehicles by merging into the next lane if possible. If you cannot merge, slow down to let them enter safely.

questions.question: You are crossing an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren and flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.
Pull to the right at the intersection and stop.
Continue through the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue through the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and/or siren, finish crossing. Then drive to the right and stop. You must yield to all emergency vehicles using lights or sirens.

questions.question: When are streets and highways most slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining hard for several hours.
When they are clean and dry.
Just after rain starts.

questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when rain first starts. The water mixes with oil and dirt on the road that has not yet washed away. Drive carefully on wet roads.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians cross here.
Side road ahead.
Railroad ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that pedestrians may be crossing the road.

questions.question: If your tires lose grip on the road, you should:

options.text: Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.
Release the gas pedal.
Brake hard and quickly.

questions.explanation: Release the gas pedal and avoid using the brakes. Do not turn until your tires grip the road again.

questions.question: If a tire blows out, you should:

options.text: Press the brake hard and hold it.
Hold the wheel firmly and brake gently.
Pull over quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the wheel firmly and brake gently.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tight to keep the car straight. Slow down gradually by releasing the gas and using gentle braking. Move to a safe spot off the road.

questions.question: If your car skids to the left, you should:

options.text: Steer to the right.
Steer to the left.
Tap the brakes lightly and shift to neutral.

questions.explanation: Remove your foot from the brake and steer in the direction you want the car to go. If the rear skids left, steer left. This straightens the car's direction.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the road edge, you should:

options.text: Slow down and carefully steer back onto the road when safe.
Turn back onto the road right away.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully steer back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: Do not turn sharply back onto the road. Instead, reduce speed, check for traffic, and gradually steer back when it is safe.
